learning_outcomes.text: The students will be familiarized with the basics of linear control engineering, modern simulation software, and automation technology.

After successful completion, the student can explain basic concepts of control engineering, apply the Laplace transform to linear and time-invariant systems, create simple mathematical models, specify and transform the associated signal flow diagram, simulate and interpret the technical system on the computer, select a suitable control structure, design the controller continuously and discretely in time using a simple method, and evaluate the performance of a control loop.

Students can apply the basics of Boolean algebra and thereby simplify digital circuits with the Karnaugh-Veitch diagram. For technical problems, they can conceive suitable automation systems and implement and simulate them based on PLC technology. For this purpose, students can work with common SIMATIC development environments (LAD, STL, FBD, and SCL) to program logic and sequence controls and perform signal processing with the PLC.

syllabus_topics: Model building, linearity, linear differential equations, step function, transient function, Laplace transform, transfer function, signal flow diagram

Rules for transformation, standard transfer elements of system theory, simulation with MATLAB/SIMULINK, control, regulation with standard control loop, examples of control loops, basic equations of the control loop, requirements, stability

Steady state, transient behavior, rules of thumb for controller adaptation, controller tuning rules, root locus, root locus method with MATLAB/SIMULINK, frequency response, Bode diagram, Nyquist criterion, frequency response methods with MATLAB/SIMULINK, discrete-time control systems
Fundamentals of device technology and control types, signals and signal transmissions, information processing
Introduction to programming of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC)
Functionality of programming languages LAD, STL, FBD, SCL, and sequence controls (state machines), as implementation using SR, sequence, or SCL
Digital implementation of control functions using Z-transformation

assessment_methods.method: Two passed laboratory exercises (prerequisite for exam)

assessment_rules: A written module exam of 120 minutes duration is required. Two passed laboratory exercises are a prerequisite for taking the exam.
